hypothesis: The exact v51 SOL Range-Onset route may retain after-cost edge under native exits, while completed-bar profit locks could reduce giveback only if they remain robust across periods and both directions.
decision: Keep the protected live SOL lifecycle unchanged. Reject a25/floor15/trail10 for SOL and do not install a40/floor15/trail20 or a60/floor15/trail30 because their pooled historical proxy gains are entirely long-side dependent and the short side is negative.

problem_restatement.input: Twenty-five exact native SOL Range-Onset lifecycles from four disjoint historical blocks plus causal one-minute SOL L2 midpoint paths.
problem_restatement.output: A report-only comparison of three frozen completed-bar profit-lock policies against the native historical controls.
problem_restatement.success_criteria: Technically complete paths, positive pooled and ex-largest-winner net, positive results on both long and short sides, and a majority of positive blocks.
problem_restatement.constraint: The current live SOL lifecycle remains an uncontaminated control and no counterfactual can alter it.

analysis: The tight 25/15/10 challenger fails pooled, long, short, ex-largest-winner, and block-robustness criteria.
The two wider challengers pass pooled and block-level criteria, but both fail the predeclared bidirectional requirement because every short slice is negative with profit factor below one.
The long-only improvement is descriptive and post-selection; installing it now would convert side analysis into an unvalidated strategy change.
The proxy preserves causal completed-minute ordering but uses midpoint OHLC, not executable quotes or exact mark-trigger timing.
uncertainties_and_failure_modes: The proxy excludes funding and any incremental exit slippage, so estimated policy net can be optimistic.
Midpoint bars cannot establish executable stop fills or mark-based trigger order within a minute.
The four blocks are disjoint but were already observed during earlier strategy research and are not untouched holdout data.
The current open long can still outperform or underperform the historical proxy policies after its exact close.
The historical long-side result could be regime-specific or winner-concentrated despite positive ex-largest-winner totals.
falsifier: Any source hash, database identity, selected-row hash, lifecycle count, side identity, fee reconstruction, minute ordering, path-completeness result, or immutable output mismatch invalidates this report. Independent forward long and short closes that make one frozen policy positive after all costs and robust across periods would update the rejection.
validation_completed: Exact four-block target-surface audit and 25 native lifecycle reconciliation.
Causal minute ordering with conflict rejection for same-timestamp midpoint rows.
Five continuity thresholds and complete 15-second paths for all 25 lifecycles.
Pooled, per-block, and per-side summaries with largest-winner removal.
Source artifact hash recheck and DuckDB file identity recheck before immutable publication.
Ten focused tests plus Ruff, formatting, diff, file-size, and function-size checks.
validation_still_required: Resolve the current native SOL lifecycle with exact exit fee, funding, slippage, and exit reason.
Collect independent current-profile long and short lifecycle comparisons without parameter changes.
If the long-only hypothesis persists, freeze it before an untouched forward window and evaluate it as a separate route rather than relabeling the bidirectional policy.
Use executable quote and exact mark-path evidence before any live stop or profit-lock proposal.

preserve_native_control.upside: Maintains a clean forward comparison and avoids a side-dependent historical transfer.
preserve_native_control.downside: The open winner can give back profit before its native exit.

install_a25_floor15_trail10.upside: Earlier profit capture on small favorable excursions.
install_a25_floor15_trail10.downside: Historical proxy loses money pooled and on both sides.

install_wider_lock_bidirectionally.upside: Positive pooled historical proxy and three positive blocks.
install_wider_lock_bidirectionally.downside: Short-side losses are substantial under both wider policies.

study_long_only_wider_lock.upside: Long proxy is positive and robust to largest-winner removal.
study_long_only_wider_lock.downside: Side selection is post-hoc and lacks untouched forward evidence.

recommendation.Recommendation: Keep the current SOL exit contract unchanged and preserve the open native lifecycle as the forward control.
recommendation.Why now: The first exact four-block causal proxy of all three frozen completed-bar locks is complete and shows material side dependence.
recommendation.Evidence reviewed: Twenty-five native lifecycles, four disjoint blocks, 178,009 SOL L2 minute inputs, five continuity thresholds, per-side/per-block economics, current live lifecycle telemetry, and immutable source identities.
recommendation.Observed problem or opportunity: Profit locks can reduce giveback, but the tested transfer damages SOL shorts and the tightest lock loses money even on longs.
recommendation.Applicable market regime: Historical Range-Onset entries across the four source blocks; current forward control is a long admitted after completed-hour crossover.
recommendation.Alternatives considered: Native control, 25/15/10, 40/15/20, 60/15/30, and a separately frozen future long-only hypothesis.
recommendation.Expected upside: Avoiding a premature bidirectional exit change preserves both capital and a clean causal forward comparison.
recommendation.Main risks and failure modes: Native giveback, proxy fill optimism, omitted funding/slippage, post-hoc side selection, and sparse forward outcomes.
recommendation.Validation completed: Exact lifecycle/source reconciliation, complete 15-second paths, causal policy mechanics, directional and block robustness, largest-winner sensitivity, and immutable publication checks.
recommendation.Validation still required: Exact current close, independent current-profile long and short closes, executable quote/mark-path replay, and a predeclared untouched side-specific window if warranted.
recommendation.Success metrics: A frozen policy must remain positive after all costs, positive without its largest winner, positive on each declared side, and positive in a majority of chronological periods.
recommendation.Failure / rollback triggers: No rollback because no change is live. Reject any future proposal on identity mismatch, path gaps, cost under-modeling, side dependence, or forward underperformance.
recommendation.Confidence level: High on the computed historical proxy rejection; low on native-exit optimality until forward lifecycles resolve.
